in_text_mentions: On examination, wasting of the thenar muscles was observed, with paresthesia over the pulp of the thumb, index, and middle fingers. The paresthesia worsened with dorsiflexion of the wrist. Active dorsiflexion of 10 degrees and palmar flexion of 20 degrees was possible in the right wrist. Radiographs revealed a volar dislocation of the lunate (spilled tea-cup sign) with an avulsion fracture of the triquetrum (Figure 1).

Our patient had a trans-triquetral fracture with lunate dislocation, classified as a greater arc perilunate injury pattern [12]. The triquetral fracture appeared to be an avulsion injury of the lunotriquetral interosseous ligament (Figure 1) [3]. Li et al. [15] reported successful management of a similar injury, treated by closed reduction of the lunate dislocation with Kirschner wire fixation across the scapholunate and lunotriquetral joints.
